CONFLICT between official Delhi pages: https://eerem.delhi.gov.in/eerem/about-delhi-solar-energy-policy still states 'Capital subsidy ... at the rate of Rs. 2,000/- per KW upto a maximum of Rs. 10,000/- per consumer' (original March 2024 notification). The solar.delhi.gov.in state-subsidy page and the Dept of Power 2nd-amendment flyer state Rs 26,000/kW up to Rs 78,000. The later amendment governs; the Gazette must settle it before publishing. Do not publish the Rs 2,000 figure.

ADDITIVE is a judgment call. The page says the State Subsidy is 'the lower of (bid cost minus the PM Surya Ghar subsidy) or Rs 26,000 x capacity, max Rs 78,000', i.e. combined central + Delhi support cannot exceed the discovered project cost. The engine cannot model a cost-linked cap, so the draft states the upper bound (Rs 78,000 at 3 kW). The UI must say 'up to'. A reviewer may prefer CONDITIONAL/CAPPED_COMBINED if the Gazette supports it; that needs a reciprocal change in the central rule.

Delivery model matters and is not encoded: the subsidy is routed through Utility-Led Aggregation / Discom Trusteeship tenders (IPGCL), first-come-first-served for the first 1.10 lakh installations up to 28 February 2027 (flyer), plus a free-installation scheme for households averaging up to 400 units/month. Confirm in the Gazette whether homeowners who install with their own vendor receive the Rs 26,000/kW.
Group Housing Societies / RWAs: Rs 11,000 per kWp (capped to the difference between plant cost and PM Surya Ghar subsidy) - not drafted (needs household count).
Generation-based incentive (Rs 3/kWh up to 3 kW etc., SOP dated 11-10-2024) is a separate benefit and is not drafted.
